weeks.label: Week 15
weeks.remark: Estimated end of Term 3 — no official calendar published yet; confirm and adjust in Admin.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Term theme: 'Buttons, Clicks & Keys'. Tour the ICT room, agree class rules, name the main parts of a computer (screen, keyboard, mouse, system unit) and switch on/log in safely.
lessons.sowResources: Interactive whiteboard, class-rules poster, printed parts-of-a-computer flashcards, BBC Bitesize KS1 'Parts of a Computer'. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Name the four main parts of a computer: screen, keyboard, mouse, system unit.
Log in to a school computer using my own class login card.
Say two ICT room rules in my own words.

plan.title: Welcome circle
plan.detail: Sit on the carpet. Show the ICT room: where to line up, where bags go, how to carry a chair. Term theme reveal: 'Buttons, Clicks & Keys'.

plan.title: Parts of a computer
plan.detail: Hold up the flashcards one at a time. Class repeats the word, then points to the real part on their own machine. Play 'Simon says point to the...'.

plan.title: Class rules together
plan.detail: Agree 4 rules: dry hands, walk not run, gentle hands on equipment, ask before printing. Each child signs the class-rules poster.

plan.title: First log in
plan.detail: Hand out login cards. Model on the big screen: type username, press Tab, type password, press Enter. Circulate - most will need the username typed with them.

plan.title: Log out and line up
plan.detail: Model the log-out routine. Everyone logs out, pushes in chairs, and says one part of the computer as the exit ticket.

activities: Login race in pairs (confident child supports partner)
successCriteria: I can point to the screen, keyboard, mouse and system unit.
I can log in with help and log out on my own.
I can name one ICT room rule.

resources.label: BBC Bitesize KS1 - Parts of a Computer

lessons.moralDescription: Take care of shared equipment and shared files - they are not just yours.
lessons.quote: A ship is safe in harbour, but that's not what ships are for.
lessons.foodForThought: Where in today's lesson could you practise stewardship?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Practise mouse control through short game-style activities. Learn point, single-click, double-click and click-and-drag.
lessons.sowResources: ABCya! Mouse Practice, ictgames.com 'Cursor Chaser', pixelthoughts.co 'Drag & Drop'. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Hold the mouse correctly with my hand resting on it.
Point and single-click on a target.
Double-click to open, and click-and-drag to move an object.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: Sit tall, feet flat. Free-explore TypingClub while the class settles.

plan.title: Mouse grip demo
plan.detail: Big-screen demo: hand rests on the mouse, index finger on the left button, wrist on the desk. Everyone copies without clicking - 'ghost practice'.

plan.title: Click and double-click
plan.detail: ABCya! Mouse Practice: point-and-click level first, then the double-click level. Say the rhythm out loud: 'tap-tap, quick!'.

plan.title: Drag and drop
plan.detail: Move to a drag-and-drop puzzle game. Rule: press, hold, move, let go. Pair weaker mouse control with a confident partner.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: Thumbs up / thumbs down: which was hardest - click, double-click or drag? Log-out routine.

successCriteria: I hold the mouse with my hand resting, not gripping.
I can single-click a small target first time.
I can drag an object where I want it.
lessons.moralDescription: Think about how your choices affect the people working near you.
lessons.quote: In the middle of difficulty lies opportunity.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed consideration - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Sign in to TypingClub with class logins. Teach good sitting posture and 'home row' hand position. Complete the first two beginner units.
lessons.sowResources: TypingClub (typingclub.com), teacher-projected posture poster, class login cards. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson) — this IS the whole lesson today.
objectives: Sign in to TypingClub with my own class login.
Sit with good typing posture: back straight, feet flat, wrists up.
Put my fingers on the home row and complete two beginner units.

plan.title: Posture chant
plan.detail: Feet flat, back straight, elbows down, eyes on the screen. Practise the pose three times before anyone touches a keyboard.

plan.title: Sign in together
plan.detail: Login cards out. Model TypingClub sign-in on the big screen, one field at a time. Circulate - the first sign-in always takes longest.

plan.title: Home row hands
plan.detail: Show the two bumps on F and J. Everyone finds them with eyes closed. Left hand ASDF, right hand JKL. Repeat the chant.

plan.title: Units 1 and 2
plan.detail: Work through the first two beginner units. Freeze the class every 5 minutes for a posture check.

plan.title: Stars and log out
plan.detail: Everyone shows their star count to a partner. Praise accuracy, not speed. Log-out routine.

successCriteria: I can sign in to TypingClub with my card.
I can find F and J without looking.
I finished two units with my fingers on the home row.
lessons.moralDescription: Good work takes time - slow down and get it right.
lessons.quote: The only real mistake is the one from which we learn nothing.
lessons.foodForThought: How would today's task go differently without patience?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Find and use the space bar, Enter and Backspace. Type single letters and their own first name.
lessons.sowResources: TypingClub, printed keyboard mat, teacher name-card exemplar. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Find the space bar, Enter and Backspace on the keyboard.
Use Backspace to fix a mistake instead of asking for help.
Type my own first name correctly.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: Straight into TypingClub for 10 minutes. Posture check at 5 minutes.

plan.title: Keyboard treasure hunt
plan.detail: Call out a key - space bar, Enter, Backspace, Shift - children point to it on the printed keyboard mat, then on the real keyboard.

plan.title: Space, Enter, Backspace
plan.detail: Open a blank document. Type letters, press space, press Enter to go down a line. Deliberately type a wrong letter and fix it with Backspace - celebrate mistakes.

plan.title: Type my name
plan.detail: Type first name. Show how Shift makes the capital letter. Model with a name card. Type it three times, each one neater than the last.

plan.title: Show a partner
plan.detail: Partner checks: is the first letter a capital? Are the letters in the right order? Log out.

successCriteria: I can find the space bar, Enter and Backspace.
I fix my own typing mistakes with Backspace.
I can type my first name with a capital letter.
lessons.moralDescription: Tell the truth about your work, including your mistakes.
lessons.quote: Small daily improvements are the key to staggering long-term results.
lessons.foodForThought: Who do you know that shows honesty well? What do they do?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Open Tux Paint (or Microsoft Paint). Choose colours, use the Brush, Stamp and Fill tools to draw a picture, then save it to the class folder.
lessons.sowResources: Tux Paint (tuxpaint.org, free) OR Microsoft Paint, teacher gallery of exemplars. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Open Tux Paint (or Microsoft Paint) from the desktop.
Use the Brush, Stamp and Fill tools to make a picture.
Save my picture into the class folder.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes of TypingClub, posture check.

plan.title: Gallery inspiration
plan.detail: Show 3 exemplar pictures. Ask: which tool made this line? Which made this shape? Introduce today's prompt: 'my favourite place'.

plan.title: Tool tour
plan.detail: Demo Brush (choose colour, change size), Stamp (pick a picture, click to place) and Fill (click inside a shape). Children copy each step on their own screen.

plan.title: Create
plan.detail: Free creation time with the prompt. Circulate and name the tools out loud as children use them: 'you used the Fill tool there'.

plan.title: Save it
plan.detail: Model saving: File > Save, type first name, click Save. Everyone saves before the log-out routine.

successCriteria: I can open the painting program by myself.
I used at least two different tools in my picture.
My picture is saved with my name on it.
lessons.moralDescription: Keep trying even when the first attempt does not work.
lessons.quote: Alone we can do so little; together we can do so much.
lessons.foodForThought: Is perseverance always easy, or does it sometimes take effort?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Practise the whole routine: log in -> open a program -> save with a sensible name -> close -> log out. Find yesterday's picture and reopen it.
lessons.sowResources: Windows File Explorer, class shared drive, printed step-by-step routine card. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Follow the whole computer routine: log in, open, save, close, log out.
Give my file a sensible name.
Find and reopen a picture I saved last week.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Routine card
plan.detail: Hand out the printed routine card. Read the 5 steps together as a chant: log in, open, save, close, log out.

plan.title: Find last week's picture
plan.detail: Open File Explorer, go to the class folder, find their own name, double-click to reopen. This is the trickiest part - pair up early finishers as helpers.

plan.title: Add and re-save
plan.detail: Add one new thing to the picture, then Save again. Discuss: the file keeps the same name, the picture is updated.

plan.title: Routine race
plan.detail: Timed run through the full 5-step routine. Everyone claps for the class, not individuals. Log out.

successCriteria: I can find my own file in the class folder.
I save my work with a name that makes sense.
I can do the whole routine with one reminder or fewer.
lessons.moralDescription: A kind word to a struggling classmate costs nothing.
lessons.quote: Whether you think you can, or you think you can't - you're right.
lessons.foodForThought: Where in today's lesson could you practise kindness?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Discuss 'if something feels wrong, tell a trusted adult'. Learn one class rule: keep private things (name, address, photos) private.
lessons.sowResources: ThinkUKnow 'Jessie & Friends' Ep. 1 (thinkuknow.co.uk), story book 'Chicken Clicking' by Jeanne Willis. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Explain that some things are private: my name, my address and my photos.
Say what to do if something online feels wrong - tell a trusted adult.
Name one trusted adult I could tell.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Jessie & Friends
plan.detail: Watch ThinkUKnow 'Jessie & Friends' Episode 1. Pause at the decision point and ask: what should she do?

plan.title: Private or share?
plan.detail: Sorting game: hold up cards (my favourite colour / my home address / my pet's name / my school photo). Class votes private or okay-to-share, then discuss.

plan.title: Trusted adults hand
plan.detail: Draw round a hand; write or draw a trusted adult on each finger. This goes into the portfolio folder.

plan.title: Class promise
plan.detail: Say the class online-safety rule together: 'If something feels wrong, I tell a trusted adult.' Log out.

successCriteria: I can name two things that should stay private.
I know to tell a trusted adult if something feels wrong.
I can name at least one trusted adult.
lessons.moralDescription: Own your work, your files and your mistakes.
lessons.quote: Good, better, best. Never let it rest until your good is better and your better is best.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed responsibility - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Print or save the best Paint picture into the personal portfolio folder. Show it to a partner and say one thing they are proud of.
lessons.sowResources: Tux Paint / Paint, class printer, printed portfolio cover sheet. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Choose my best piece of work and say why it is my best.
Save or print it into my portfolio folder.
Tell a partner one thing I am proud of.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Choosing my best
plan.detail: Open the class folder and look at all their pictures. Sentence stem on the board: 'I chose this one because...'.

plan.title: Tidy it up
plan.detail: Open the chosen picture and improve one thing - a colour, a missing detail, a title stamp. Save it again.

plan.title: Into the portfolio
plan.detail: Print (or save to the portfolio folder). Stick the printed cover sheet on the front and write their name on it.

plan.title: Proud partners
plan.detail: Turn to a partner: 'I am proud of... because...'. Two or three share with the whole class. Log out.

successCriteria: I chose a piece of work and gave a reason.
My work is in my portfolio folder with my name.
I told a partner one thing I am proud of.
lessons.moralDescription: Ask 'why' and 'what if' - that is where real learning starts.
lessons.quote: A goal without a plan is just a wish.
lessons.foodForThought: How would today's task go differently without curiosity?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Rotate through 4 short stations: mouse game, TypingClub, Paint drawing, log-in-and-save race. Teacher observes and ticks off the skills checklist.
lessons.sowResources: Skills checklist per pupil, station cards, timer. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Move sensibly between four ICT stations.
Show the skills I have learned this term without being told each step.
Ask for help using words, not just a raised hand.

plan.title: Station briefing
plan.detail: Explain the four stations and the rotation signal (timer bell). Groups of 4-5, 12 minutes per station.

plan.title: Station 1 - Mouse game
plan.detail: Click and drag accuracy game. Observe grip and control, tick the checklist.

plan.title: Station 2 - TypingClub
plan.detail: Independent unit work. Observe posture and home-row hand position.

plan.title: Station 3 - Paint
plan.detail: Free drawing with at least two tools. Observe tool choice and independence.

plan.title: Station 4 - Log in and save race
plan.detail: Full routine from log-in to save. Observe who still needs the routine card.

plan.title: Checklist reveal
plan.detail: Show each child their ticked checklist. Name one thing to practise next week. Log out.

successCriteria: I moved between stations quietly when the timer went.
I did each station task without step-by-step help.
I know one thing to practise next week.
lessons.moralDescription: Respect other people's work, ideas and privacy.
lessons.quote: Character is doing the right thing when nobody's looking.
lessons.foodForThought: Who do you know that shows respect well? What do they do?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Whole-class recap: name the parts, log in, open a program, save, log out. Rehearse the practical task in pairs.
lessons.sowResources: Recap slide deck, practice task cards, TypingClub. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Recall the parts of the computer and the log-in routine.
Complete the practical task steps in the right order.
Say one online-safety rule out loud, clearly.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Quickfire recap
plan.detail: Slide recap: point to the part, name it, chant the 5-step routine, say the safety rule together.

plan.title: Rehearse the practical
plan.detail: In pairs, one child does the exam task while the partner reads the task card aloud, then swap. Task: log in, open Paint, draw a guided picture, save with own name, log out.

plan.title: Trouble spots
plan.detail: Reteach the two steps most children fumbled - usually saving with the right name, and finding the program icon.

plan.title: Safety rule rehearsal
plan.detail: Each child practises saying their safety rule to a partner in one clear sentence. Log out.

successCriteria: I can do the practical steps in order with a partner reading them.
I can save a file with my own name.
I can say one online-safety rule in a full sentence.
lessons.moralDescription: The best projects are built by people who help each other.
lessons.quote: Well begun is half done.
lessons.foodForThought: Is cooperation always easy, or does it sometimes take effort?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Individual observation: log in, open Paint, complete a short guided drawing, save the file with own name, log out. Answer one online-safety question aloud.
lessons.sowResources: Observation checklist (from HTML curriculum: 'logs in, controls the mouse, saves a picture; gives one online-safety rule out loud'), assessment rubric.
objectives: Complete the Term 1 practical task on my own.
Save my work with my own name.
Answer one online-safety question out loud.

plan.title: Settle and explain
plan.detail: Calm start. Explain: this is a 'show me what you can do' task, not a test to worry about. Everyone gets a turn.

plan.title: Group A practical
plan.detail: First group works through the task while the rest do independent TypingClub. Observe against the checklist.

plan.title: Group B practical
plan.detail: Second group. Same task, same checklist.

plan.title: Group C practical
plan.detail: Third group. Same task, same checklist.

plan.title: Safety question + close
plan.detail: One-to-one: 'Tell me one rule for staying safe online.' Record the answer. Praise every child by name.

activities: Individual observed practical: log in, open Paint, guided drawing, save, log out
successCriteria: I logged in by myself.
I controlled the mouse to complete the drawing.
I saved the picture with my name and logged out.
I gave one online-safety rule out loud.
lessons.moralDescription: Small, steady effort beats a rushed burst at the end.
lessons.quote: It always seems impossible until it's done.
lessons.foodForThought: Where in today's lesson could you practise diligence?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Plan a 4-page 'All About Me' picture book. Sketch on paper first: page 1 = my name, page 2 = my family, page 3 = my pet or favourite toy, page 4 = things I like.
lessons.sowResources: Printed storyboard sheet, coloured pencils. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Plan a 4-page book before I start on the computer.
Decide what goes on each page.
Sketch my ideas on the storyboard sheet.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Look at a real book
plan.detail: Share a simple picture book. Notice: each page has one idea and one picture. Show the finished teacher exemplar of 'My First Digital Book'.

plan.title: The four pages
plan.detail: Page 1 = my name. Page 2 = my family. Page 3 = my pet or favourite toy. Page 4 = things I like. Write the four headings on the board.

plan.title: Storyboard time
plan.detail: Sketch all four pages on paper with coloured pencils. No computers this lesson - planning first is the whole point. Circulate and ask 'what will you draw here?'.

plan.title: Tell your plan
plan.detail: Partners describe their four pages to each other. Collect storyboards in for next week.

successCriteria: My storyboard has all four pages sketched.
Each page has one clear idea.
I can tell a partner what each page will show.
lessons.moralDescription: Sharing unfinished work for feedback takes courage - and pays off.
lessons.quote: The expert in anything was once a beginner.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed courage - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Use Tux Paint / Paint to draw each of the 4 pages. Save each drawing with a clear name: page1.png, page2.png etc.
lessons.sowResources: Tux Paint / Paint, class shared drive. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Draw each page of my book using the paint tools.
Save each page with a clear name: page1, page2, page3, page4.
Follow my own plan from last week.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Plans back out
plan.detail: Return the storyboards. Model naming: page1, page2 - no capitals, no spaces. Write the naming rule on the board.

plan.title: Draw and save
plan.detail: Draw page by page, saving each one before starting the next. Rule on the board: 'finish a page, save a page'. Most children manage 2-3 pages today.

plan.title: Check the folder
plan.detail: Open the class folder and check the file names are right. Fix any that are wrong together. Log out.

successCriteria: My drawings match my plan.
Each page is saved separately.
My file names follow the page1, page2 rule.
lessons.moralDescription: Notice and thank the people who help you learn.
lessons.quote: Success is the sum of small efforts, repeated day in and day out.
lessons.foodForThought: How would today's task go differently without gratitude?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Open a blank Word document. Type a one-line title under each page. Use the Shift key for the capital letter at the start.
lessons.sowResources: Microsoft Word, keyboard mat, teacher exemplar page. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Open a blank Word document.
Type a one-line title for each page.
Use the Shift key to make a capital letter at the start.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Shift key demo
plan.detail: Show the exemplar title page. Demo: hold Shift, press the letter, let go. Practise 'A a A a' in the air, then on screen.

plan.title: Open Word and set up
plan.detail: Open a blank document, type name at the top, press Enter twice. Model on the big screen at pupil pace.

plan.title: Type the four titles
plan.detail: One title per line, each starting with a capital. Backspace to fix mistakes. Support: printed title strips to copy from.

plan.title: Save and share
plan.detail: Save as titles.docx into their folder. Partner reads the titles aloud to check they make sense. Log out.

successCriteria: I opened a new Word document by myself.
I typed a title for each of my four pages.
Each title starts with a capital letter.
lessons.moralDescription: Do the right thing even when nobody is checking.
lessons.quote: Do not wait for the perfect moment. Take the moment and make it perfect.
lessons.foodForThought: Who do you know that shows integrity well? What do they do?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Present the finished picture book to a small group. Give one 'star' (something you liked) to a friend. Save the completed portfolio.
lessons.sowResources: Class projector, printed star stickers, portfolio folder. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Present my digital book to a small group.
Give a friend one 'star' - something I liked about their book.
Save my finished work into the portfolio folder.

plan.title: Rehearse with a partner
plan.detail: Practise the sentence: 'This is my book. My favourite page is ___ because ___.'

plan.title: Show and tell
plan.detail: Groups of five at the projector or around a screen. Each child gets two minutes. Audience sits with hands still and eyes on the speaker.

plan.title: Star stickers
plan.detail: After each presenter, one listener gives a star: 'I liked ___'. Everyone gets at least one star sticker.

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: Save all four pages plus the titles document into the portfolio folder. Check the folder together on the big screen.

plan.title: Term celebration
plan.detail: Look back at Week 1. Name three things they can do now that they could not in August. Log out.

successCriteria: I presented my book using two full sentences.
I gave a friend a kind, specific compliment.
All my work is in my portfolio folder.
lessons.moralDescription: The best learners admit what they do not know yet.
lessons.quote: The only way to do great work is to love what you do.
lessons.foodForThought: Is humility always easy, or does it sometimes take effort?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Term theme: 'Typing & Documents'. Recap logging in, saving and the ICT room rules. Introduce this term's goal: type a formatted paragraph and save it in BOTH Word and Google Docs.
lessons.sowResources: Term overview slide, class-rules poster, TypingClub sign-in cards. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Log in and open a program without step-by-step help.
Explain what we will make this term: a formatted document saved in two places.
Set my own TypingClub target for the term.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: Sign in, posture check, free practice while the class settles.

plan.title: Term reveal
plan.detail: Term theme: 'Typing & Documents'. Show the finished exemplar fact card they will make by Week 15. Explain the two-tool idea: Microsoft AND Google.

plan.title: Rules and routine recap
plan.detail: Recap the ICT room rules and the 5-step routine from Year 1. Quickfire: who can log in, open Word and close it in under 2 minutes?

plan.title: Diagnostic task
plan.detail: Type one sentence about the holidays, save it with own name. Note who needs support with typing, saving or the mouse - this sets the groupings for the term.

plan.title: My target
plan.detail: Each pupil writes their TypingClub target on the goal sheet (a star count or a level). Stick to the wall chart. Log out.

successCriteria: I logged in and opened a program on my own.
I typed and saved a sentence with my name on it.
I have written my typing target on the chart.
lessons.moralDescription: Think about how your choices affect the people working near you.
lessons.quote: Good, better, best. Never let it rest until your good is better and your better is best.
lessons.foodForThought: Where in today's lesson could you practise consideration?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Focus on home-row rhythm and accuracy — quality before speed. Aim to finish TypingClub Level 1 by half term.
lessons.sowResources: TypingClub, wall chart of class accuracy stars. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Keep my fingers on the home row while typing.
Choose accuracy before speed.
Reach the end of TypingClub Level 1 by half term.

plan.title: Hands ready
plan.detail: F and J bumps, elbows down, eyes on screen. 60-second warm-up drill on the home row only.

plan.title: Rhythm, not race
plan.detail: Model typing slowly with an even beat, then fast and messy. Ask which one scored better. Rule for the term: 'smooth beats fast'.

plan.title: TypingClub units
plan.detail: Independent unit work towards Level 1. Freeze for a posture check every 5 minutes. Support: cover hands with a card for children who peek.

plan.title: Accuracy stars
plan.detail: Each pupil records today's best accuracy on the wall chart. Celebrate anyone above 90% regardless of speed.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: Which letter is hardest to reach? Show it on the keyboard mat and practise ten times. Log out.

successCriteria: My fingers start and return to the home row.
My accuracy is 90% or better in at least one lesson.
I typed without looking down for a whole exercise.
lessons.moralDescription: Good work takes time - slow down and get it right.
lessons.quote: A goal without a plan is just a wish.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed patience - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.subtopic: Word vs Google Docs — A Quick Tour
lessons.outline: Open both Microsoft Word and Google Docs. Compare: same job, two tools. Type own name in each and save.
lessons.sowResources: Microsoft Word (school licence), Google Docs (Google Workspace for Education, free), Drive vs OneDrive comparison poster. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Open both Microsoft Word and Google Docs.
Explain that two different tools can do the same job.
Type and save my name in each one.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Two tools, one job
plan.detail: Side-by-side on the big screen: Word and Docs. Spot the same buttons in both. Analogy: two shops that both sell bread.

plan.title: Word first
plan.detail: Open Word, type full name, make it big, save to OneDrive as name_word.docx. Model each step, pupils copy.

plan.title: Then Docs
plan.detail: Open Docs in the browser, type the same name. Notice: Docs saves by itself - there is no Save button. Rename the document to name_docs.

plan.title: Spot the difference
plan.detail: Class list: what was the same, what was different? Record on the comparison poster. Log out.

activities: Type and rename in Google Docs
successCriteria: I opened Word and Google Docs by myself.
I typed my name in both.
I can say one difference between them.
lessons.moralDescription: Tell the truth about your work, including your mistakes.
lessons.quote: Character is doing the right thing when nobody's looking.
lessons.foodForThought: How would today's task go differently without honesty?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Type a 3-4 sentence paragraph about 'My Weekend' in both Word and Docs. Use full stops and the space bar correctly.
lessons.sowResources: Word · Docs, printed prompt card, teacher exemplar paragraph. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Type a paragraph of 3-4 sentences.
Use full stops and single spaces correctly.
Save the same paragraph in Word and in Docs.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up

Accept or reject suggestions on my own work with a reason.
Explain the difference between editing and suggesting.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up

plan.title: Suggesting vs editing

plan.title: Peer edit

plan.title: Accept or reject
plan.detail: Back to your own report. For each suggestion, accept or reject and say why to your partner. Rejecting with a good reason is a success, not a failure.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: Which suggestion improved the report most? Save and log out.

successCriteria: I made three specific suggestions on a partner's report.
I accepted or rejected each suggestion on mine with a reason.
I can explain the difference between suggesting and editing.

Present my report to a small group in two minutes.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Term theme: 'Code a Gadget'. Set a personal words-per-minute goal in TypingClub. Preview the term project: a working micro:bit gadget.

objectives: Set a personal words-per-minute goal in TypingClub.
Describe what a micro:bit is and what it can do.
Explain what the term project will be.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: Sign in, baseline WPM run, posture check.

plan.title: Unboxing the micro:bit
plan.detail: Pass round a micro:bit. Do not plug anything in yet - handling rules first: hold by the edges, never by the pins, no bending.

plan.title: What could we build?
plan.detail: Show short clips of finished projects: step counter, reaction game, light meter. Class brainstorms what the device must sense to do each one.

plan.title: Baseline and goal
plan.detail: Record baseline WPM. Set a personal goal on the goal sheet - realistic, about +5 WPM by half term.

plan.title: Term map
plan.detail: Walk through the term: blocks first, then loops, then conditions, then build a gadget. Log out.

successCriteria: I can handle a micro:bit safely.
I recorded my baseline WPM and set a goal.
I can name two things a micro:bit can sense.
lessons.moralDescription: Keep trying even when the first attempt does not work.
lessons.quote: Kind words can be short and easy to speak, but their echoes are truly endless.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Explore the micro:bit hardware: LEDs, buttons, sensors (light, temp, accelerometer). Identify inputs vs outputs on a labelling sheet.
lessons.sowResources: micro:bit V2 devices (one per pair), USB cables, printed labelling sheet, micro:bit intro video (youtube.com/@microbit_edu). TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Identify the main parts of the micro:bit: LEDs, buttons, sensors, pins.
Sort features into inputs and outputs.
Explain the difference between an input and an output.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Input or output?
plan.detail: Definition first: input goes in to the computer, output comes out. Sort classroom examples (keyboard, screen, speaker, microphone) before touching the micro:bit.

plan.title: Label the board
plan.detail: In pairs with the labelling sheet: 25 LEDs, buttons A and B, light sensor, temperature sensor, accelerometer, compass, radio, pins, USB, battery socket.

plan.title: Sort them
plan.detail: Colour-code the labelling sheet: inputs in one colour, outputs in another. Discuss the tricky ones - the pins can be both.

plan.title: Quickfire
plan.detail: Teacher names a part, class shouts input or output. Devices counted back in. Log out.

successCriteria: I can point to the buttons, LEDs and sensors.
I sorted the features into inputs and outputs.
I can explain the difference in my own words.
lessons.moralDescription: A kind word to a struggling classmate costs nothing.
lessons.quote: Honesty is the first chapter in the book of wisdom.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed kindness - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Sign in to makecode.microbit.org. Drag blocks to show a heart, then a name. FIRST-TIME TEACHER TIP: toggle to the Python view to see the same code as text — pupils compare.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode Editor (makecode.microbit.org, free), first-time-teacher video: 'micro:bit lesson 1' by micro:bit Educational Foundation, printed cheat sheet. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Sign in to MakeCode and start a new project.
Drag blocks to show an icon on the LED display.
Download my program onto the micro:bit.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Tour MakeCode
plan.detail: Sign in to makecode.microbit.org. Show the three areas: simulator on the left, block palette in the middle, workspace on the right.

plan.title: First program
plan.detail: 'on start' + 'show icon' (heart). Test in the simulator first, then Download and copy to the MICROBIT drive. Do the transfer step slowly together - it is the fiddly part.

plan.title: Show a name
plan.detail: Add 'show string' with their own name. Notice the letters scroll. Try changing the scroll speed.

plan.title: Peek at Python
plan.detail: Toggle the Blocks/Python switch. Same program, written as text. Do not teach the syntax yet - just plant the idea that blocks are code. Log out.

activities: Show icon and download to device
successCriteria: I made a program that shows an icon.
I downloaded it onto the physical micro:bit.
I have seen my program written as Python text.
lessons.moralDescription: Own your work, your files and your mistakes.
lessons.quote: The way to get started is to quit talking and begin doing.
lessons.foodForThought: How would today's task go differently without responsibility?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Program: 'when button A pressed -> show heart', 'when button B pressed -> show ghost'. Compare Blocks and Python side-by-side in MakeCode.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, micro:bit, printed 'onButtonPressed' Python vs Blocks reference. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Use 'on button A pressed' and 'on button B pressed' as event blocks.
Explain what an event is.
Compare the same program in Blocks and in Python.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What is an event?
plan.detail: An event is something that happens which the program waits for. Real-world examples: doorbell, alarm, hand raised.

plan.title: Two buttons, two icons
plan.detail: Build: on button A show heart, on button B show ghost. Test in the simulator, then on the device.

plan.title: Add A+B
plan.detail: Extend with 'on button A+B pressed' showing a third icon. Challenge: make it show a message instead.

plan.title: Side-by-side
plan.detail: Toggle to Python. Match each block to its line using the printed reference. Which parts look the same? Log out.

successCriteria: My program responds to both buttons.
I can explain what an event is.
I can point to the Python line that matches a block.
lessons.moralDescription: Ask 'why' and 'what if' - that is where real learning starts.
lessons.quote: You miss 100 percent of the shots you don't take.
lessons.foodForThought: Who do you know that shows curiosity well? What do they do?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Use a 'forever' loop and a 'repeat X times' loop to make an LED animation. Explain in own words what a loop does.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, micro:bit, loop-challenge cards (5 challenges from easy to tricky). TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Use a 'forever' loop and a 'repeat X times' loop.
Explain in my own words what a loop does.
Build an LED animation using a loop.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Loops all around us
plan.detail: Non-computer examples: brushing teeth (repeat), a fan (forever). Difference: repeat has a count, forever does not stop.

plan.title: Animate
plan.detail: Show heart, pause 500ms, show small heart, pause 500ms - inside a forever loop. The pause is essential; without it the animation is invisible.

plan.title: Loop challenge cards
plan.detail: Five challenge cards from easy to tricky: count to 5, flash three times, chase an LED across the row, blink faster each time.

plan.title: Explain it
plan.detail: Partner explanation using the stem: 'This loop repeats ___ because ___.' Log out.

successCriteria: My animation uses a loop with pauses.
I completed at least three challenge cards.
I can explain the difference between forever and repeat.
lessons.moralDescription: Respect other people's work, ideas and privacy.
lessons.quote: Fall seven times, stand up eight.
lessons.foodForThought: Is respect always easy, or does it sometimes take effort?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: React to a sensor: 'if shake -> show surprised face' or 'if light level < 50 -> show moon'. Test in the classroom vs a dark cupboard.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, micro:bit, printed if-block reference, torch for testing. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Use an if block to react to a sensor.
Set a sensible threshold value.
Test my program in two different conditions.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: If, then
plan.detail: Everyday conditions: if it rains, take an umbrella. Introduce the if block shape and the comparison operator.

plan.title: Shake to react
plan.detail: Build: on shake, show a surprised face. Test by shaking. Then extend: if light level < 50, show a moon.

plan.title: Find your threshold
plan.detail: Read the live light level in the classroom and inside a cupboard or under a book. Choose a threshold between the two readings. This is real testing.

plan.title: Demo
plan.detail: Two pairs demo their light-sensing gadget with the torch. Log out.

successCriteria: My program uses an if block with a sensor.
My threshold value is based on real readings.
My gadget behaves differently in light and dark.
lessons.moralDescription: The best projects are built by people who help each other.
lessons.quote: What we learn with pleasure we never forget.
lessons.foodForThought: Where in today's lesson could you practise cooperation?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.subtopic: Build a Gadget — Pick a Project
lessons.outline: Choose ONE gadget to build: (a) step counter, (b) mood badge, (c) light meter, (d) reaction-time game. Plan on paper first.
lessons.sowResources: Project brief cards (4 options), planning sheet, MakeCode. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Choose one gadget project and justify my choice.
Plan the inputs, outputs and steps on paper.
Predict which blocks I will need.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: The four briefs
plan.detail: Read the project cards: step counter, mood badge, light meter, reaction-time game. For each, ask: what is the input, what is the output?

plan.title: Choose and justify
plan.detail: Pairs choose one and write two sentences on why. Steer strong pairs to the reaction game, developing pairs to the mood badge.

plan.title: Plan on paper
plan.detail: Planning sheet: inputs, outputs, what happens first, what repeats, what condition decides. No coding today - the plan is the deliverable.

plan.title: Plan check
plan.detail: Teacher initials each plan before pairs may start coding next week. Log out.

activities: Read and analyse four project briefs
Paper plan with inputs and outputs
successCriteria: My pair has chosen a project and can say why.
My plan names the inputs and outputs.
My plan says which blocks will repeat and which will decide.
lessons.moralDescription: Small, steady effort beats a rushed burst at the end.
lessons.quote: Learning never exhausts the mind.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed diligence - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.subtopic: Build a Gadget — First Working Version
lessons.outline: Build a working v1 of the chosen gadget. Test with a partner. Save the code with a clear file name.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, micro:bit, class shared drive for .hex files. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Build a working first version of my gadget.
Test it with a partner and note what does not work.
Save my code with a clear file name.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Version 1 rules
plan.detail: V1 does the main job only. No sounds, no animations, no extras. Getting one thing working beats five half-things.

plan.title: Build
plan.detail: Pairs build from their plan. Circulate: ask 'show me it working' rather than looking at the code. Struggling pairs get a starter file.

plan.title: Partner test and save
plan.detail: Swap devices with another pair and try to use the gadget without instructions. Note what confused them. Save as project_v1. Log out.

successCriteria: My gadget does its main job.
Another pair tested it and I wrote down their feedback.
My code is saved as project_v1.
lessons.moralDescription: Sharing unfinished work for feedback takes courage - and pays off.
lessons.quote: Genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration.
lessons.foodForThought: How would today's task go differently without courage?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Add ONE improvement (e.g. a sound effect, a reset button, a starting animation). Log the change in a paper 'dev diary'.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, printed dev-diary template. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Add one improvement to my gadget.
Record the change in a dev diary.
Explain why I chose that improvement.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Read the feedback
plan.detail: Re-read last week's tester feedback. Choose ONE improvement that fixes a real problem, not just a decoration.

plan.title: Implement one change
plan.detail: Add the improvement: a sound effect, a reset button, a start-up animation, or clearer output. Keep v1 saved - save this as v2.

plan.title: Dev diary
plan.detail: Complete the diary entry: what I changed, why, and whether it worked.

plan.title: Show the difference
plan.detail: Demo v1 then v2 to the pair who tested it. Log out.

successCriteria: My gadget has one clear improvement.
My dev diary explains what and why.
Both v1 and v2 are saved.
lessons.moralDescription: Notice and thank the people who help you learn.
lessons.quote: Do the best you can until you know better. Then, when you know better, do better.
lessons.foodForThought: Who do you know that shows gratitude well? What do they do?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Practise explaining code to a partner using the sentence stems: 'This block means…', 'This loop repeats…', 'This if-block checks…'. Prepare for the exam.
lessons.sowResources: Sentence-stem cards, peer-explanation checklist, TypingClub. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Explain my code to a partner using the sentence stems.
Point out where the loop and the condition are.
Answer a question about my code without reading from the screen.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Model a good explanation
plan.detail: Teacher explains a sample program using the stems: 'This block means...', 'This loop repeats...', 'This if-block checks...'. Then a deliberately vague version - class spots the difference.

plan.title: Explain in pairs
plan.detail: Two rounds: explain your code to a partner, get scored on the peer checklist, then swap. Second round should be noticeably better.

plan.title: Teacher questions
plan.detail: Circulate asking one exam-style question each: 'What happens if I remove this block?', 'Where does the program start?'

plan.title: Weak spots
plan.detail: Each pupil notes the question they found hardest. Log out.

successCriteria: I explained my whole program using the sentence stems.
I can point to the loop and the condition.
I answered a question about my code without reading it out.
lessons.moralDescription: Do the right thing even when nobody is checking.
lessons.quote: A ship is safe in harbour, but that's not what ships are for.
lessons.foodForThought: Is integrity always easy, or does it sometimes take effort?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Individual practical: build a small micro:bit program using at least one loop and one condition. Demonstrate it working; explain the code to the teacher.
lessons.sowResources: Marking rubric — from HTML: 'a working micro:bit gadget in Python using at least one loop and one condition'.
objectives: Build a micro:bit program using at least one loop and one condition.
Demonstrate it working on the physical device.
Explain my code to the teacher.

plan.title: Brief
plan.detail: Read the task. Requirements on the board: at least one loop, at least one condition, must run on the device.

plan.title: Build
plan.detail: Individual build (paired devices, individual code). Silent conditions. Technical help only - no design help.

plan.title: Demonstrate
plan.detail: Called one at a time to demo the working device while others continue or extend.

plan.title: Explain
plan.detail: One-to-one: point to your loop, point to your condition, say what each does. Recorded on the rubric.

plan.title: Save and close
plan.detail: Save the .hex with the correct name. Devices counted in. Log out.

successCriteria: My program uses at least one loop.
My program uses at least one condition.
It runs on the physical micro:bit.
I explained my code clearly.
lessons.moralDescription: The best learners admit what they do not know yet.
lessons.quote: In the middle of difficulty lies opportunity.
lessons.foodForThought: Where in today's lesson could you practise humility?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Learn 'radio send' and 'radio receive' blocks. Two micro:bits send a heart to each other when a button is pressed.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, 2 micro:bits per pair, radio-blocks reference. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Use radio send and radio receive blocks.
Set the same radio group on both devices.
Send a message from one micro:bit to another.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: How radio works
plan.detail: Both micro:bits must be on the same radio group - like tuning two walkie-talkies to the same channel. Assign each pair a group number to avoid chaos.

plan.title: Send and receive
plan.detail: Program: on start set radio group; on button A, radio send number 1; on radio received, show heart. Flash BOTH devices with the same program.

plan.title: Troubleshoot
plan.detail: Common faults: different group numbers, only one device flashed, battery not connected. Work through the fault-finding list together.

plan.title: Pair up across the room
plan.detail: Test how far apart the devices still work. Log out.

successCriteria: Both my micro:bits are on the same radio group.
Pressing a button on one shows something on the other.
I can name one reason radio might not work.
lessons.moralDescription: Give credit where it's due, and take feedback the same way you'd give it.
lessons.quote: The only real mistake is the one from which we learn nothing.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed fairness - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Extend the radio project: send different messages for buttons A, B and A+B. Display the received message on the second micro:bit.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, 2 micro:bits per pair, project brief. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Send different messages for buttons A, B and A+B.
Display the received message clearly.
Test my chat gadget with another pair.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Message plan
plan.detail: Decide what each button means: A = yes, B = no, A+B = hello. Write the code table on paper first.

plan.title: Build the chat gadget
plan.detail: Three send events, and a receive handler that shows the right icon or string for each value. This needs an if/else if chain - link back to Week 6.

plan.title: Cross-pair test
plan.detail: Swap one device with another pair on the same group and hold a conversation. Log out.

successCriteria: My gadget sends three different messages.
The receiving device shows the right thing for each.
Another pair could understand my messages.
lessons.moralDescription: Doing the boring warm-up daily is what makes the fun part possible.

lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, 2 micro:bits, bug log template. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)

Log the bug and the fix.
Add one polish feature.

plan.title: Fix the bugs

plan.title: One polish feature

plan.title: Bug of the week
plan.detail: Share the most interesting bug found and how it was fixed. Log out.

successCriteria: I tested my gadget against a test list.
I fixed at least one bug and logged it.
My gadget has one polish feature.
