plan.title: What is a variable?
plan.detail: A labelled box that holds a value you can change. Physical demo: a box labelled 'score' with cards swapped in and out.

plan.title: Make a counter
plan.detail: set score to 0; on button A pressed, change score by 1; show number score. Test - this is the single most useful pattern of the term.

plan.title: Reset and limits
plan.detail: Add button B to reset the score to 0. Challenge: use an if-block so the score cannot go above 10.

plan.title: Python check
plan.detail: Toggle to Python: spot score = 0 and score += 1. Log out.

successCriteria: My program has a variable with a starting value.
The variable changes when I press a button.
The current value is shown on the display.
lessons.moralDescription: Ask 'why' and 'what if' - that is where real learning starts.
lessons.quote: Do the best you can until you know better. Then, when you know better, do better.
lessons.foodForThought: How would today's task go differently without curiosity?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Bring loops and if-blocks together: a program that keeps checking the temperature and shows different faces at different thresholds.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, micro:bit, worked-example cards, first-time-teacher video: 'micro:bit temperature project' (Craig 'n Dave). TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Combine a loop with if / else if conditions.
Use a sensor reading to choose between three outcomes.
Test each branch of my program.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Three-way decisions
plan.detail: Walk through the worked example: cold below 25, warm 25-30, hot above 30. Draw the decision as a flowchart on the board.

plan.title: Build the thermometer
plan.detail: forever loop, read temperature, if/else if/else showing three different faces. Order matters - discuss why checking 'hot' first changes the behaviour.

plan.title: Test every branch
plan.detail: Cold: hold near the window or press a cold object to the chip. Hot: cup it in both hands. Every branch must be seen to work.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: Why does the order of the conditions matter? Log out.

successCriteria: My program uses a loop and at least three branches.
I saw every branch work on the device.
I can explain why condition order matters.
lessons.moralDescription: Respect other people's work, ideas and privacy.
lessons.quote: A ship is safe in harbour, but that's not what ships are for.
lessons.foodForThought: Who do you know that shows respect well? What do they do?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Send messages between two micro:bits using the radio blocks. Build a 'ping-pong' game: A sends '1', B sends '2', repeat.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, 2 micro:bits per pair, radio-blocks reference. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Send and receive numbers between two micro:bits.
Build a two-device ping-pong game.
Explain why both devices need the same radio group.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Radio recap
plan.detail: Same group = same channel. Assign group numbers per pair. Both devices get the SAME program.

plan.title: Ping-pong build
plan.detail: On button A send 1; on received 1, show arrow and send 2 back; on received 2, show a different arrow. Watch the message bounce between devices.

plan.title: Add a counter
plan.detail: Add a variable that counts how many times the message has bounced. Links Week 3 to today.

plan.title: Debug together
plan.detail: Common faults: only one device flashed, group mismatch, infinite loop of messages. Log out.

successCriteria: Messages travel both ways between the devices.
My program uses a variable to count bounces.
I can fix a radio group mismatch.
lessons.moralDescription: The best projects are built by people who help each other.
lessons.quote: In the middle of difficulty lies opportunity.
lessons.foodForThought: Is cooperation always easy, or does it sometimes take effort?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Choose ONE project idea from a menu: fitness tracker, distance messenger, class attendance signaller, mini-quiz device. Plan on paper — features, inputs, outputs.
lessons.sowResources: Project menu card (4 options), planning sheet, MakeCode. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Choose a project and list its features.
Identify the inputs and outputs for each feature.
Produce a plan a partner could build from.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: The project menu
plan.detail: Fitness tracker, distance messenger, attendance signaller, mini-quiz device. For each, discuss what would be hard and what would be satisfying.

plan.title: Feature thinking
plan.detail: A feature is one thing the device does for the user. Break each project idea into three features - this is the planning skill being assessed.

plan.title: Write the plan
plan.detail: Planning sheet: project name, who it is for, three features, inputs, outputs, variables needed.

plan.title: Swap and test the plan
plan.detail: Give your plan to another pair. Could they build from it? Clarify anything they questioned. Log out.

activities: Break the project into three features
successCriteria: My plan names three specific features.
I have listed the inputs, outputs and variables.
Another pair understood my plan.
lessons.moralDescription: Small, steady effort beats a rushed burst at the end.
lessons.quote: The only real mistake is the one from which we learn nothing.
lessons.foodForThought: Where in today's lesson could you practise diligence?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Implement the first main feature. Save with clear file name (project_v1.hex). Test with a partner.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, micro:bit, class shared drive. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Implement the first feature of my project.
Test it before adding anything else.
Save the code as project_v1.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: One feature at a time
plan.detail: Rule for the build: get feature 1 working and saved before touching feature 2. Explain why - if everything breaks at once you cannot find the cause.

plan.title: Build feature 1
plan.detail: Independent build from the plan. Circulate and ask 'show me it working'. Keep a shared board of solutions to problems that come up more than once.

plan.title: Test and save
plan.detail: Partner tests feature 1 against the plan. Save as project_v1. Log out.

successCriteria: Feature 1 works on the physical device.
A partner tested it against my plan.
My code is saved as project_v1.
lessons.moralDescription: Sharing unfinished work for feedback takes courage - and pays off.
lessons.quote: Small daily improvements are the key to staggering long-term results.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed courage - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Add a second feature to the build. Test again with a partner. Save as v2.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, micro:bit, version-control notes card. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Add a second feature without breaking the first.
Re-test both features together.
Save as project_v2 and keep v1.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Why keep old versions?
plan.detail: If v2 breaks badly you can go back to v1. Show the version-control notes card. Professional habit, taught early.

plan.title: Build feature 2
plan.detail: Add the second feature. Re-test feature 1 afterwards - it often breaks, and noticing that is the learning.

plan.title: Test both and save
plan.detail: Test both features in one run. Save as project_v2. Log out.

successCriteria: Both features work in the same program.
I checked feature 1 still works.
I have v1 and v2 saved separately.
lessons.moralDescription: Notice and thank the people who help you learn.
lessons.quote: Alone we can do so little; together we can do so much.
lessons.foodForThought: How would today's task go differently without gratitude?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Practise explaining the whole program to a partner: what the variables do, where the loops are, what each if-block checks.
lessons.sowResources: Sentence-stem cards, peer-explanation rubric, TypingClub. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Explain my whole program to a partner.
Say what each variable holds and where it changes.
Identify every loop and condition in my code.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Model the explanation
plan.detail: Teacher explains a sample project well, then badly. Class scores both against the rubric so the standard is clear.

plan.title: Explain in pairs
plan.detail: Two rounds with feedback in between. The rubric rewards naming variables, loops and conditions specifically.

plan.title: Teacher questioning
plan.detail: One-to-one exam-style questions: 'What happens if the user presses B twice?', 'Where does the score get reset?'

plan.title: Target setting
plan.detail: Each pupil writes one thing to explain better next time. Log out.

successCriteria: I explained my program without reading the screen.
I named my variables and said what they hold.
I pointed out every loop and condition.
lessons.moralDescription: Do the right thing even when nobody is checking.
lessons.quote: Whether you think you can, or you think you can't - you're right.
lessons.foodForThought: Who do you know that shows integrity well? What do they do?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Debug 4 teacher-made 'broken' programs. Identify the bug, propose the fix, then apply and re-test.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, printed buggy-code sheets, teacher exemplar solutions. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Find the bug in a broken program.
Propose a fix before changing anything.
Apply the fix and re-test.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Debugging method
plan.detail: Read the code, predict what it should do, run it, compare, then change ONE thing. Predict-run-compare beats random clicking.

plan.title: Debug marathon
plan.detail: Four broken programs, 10 minutes each: a loop with no pause, a variable never reset, an if/else if in the wrong order, a radio group mismatch. Write the diagnosis before fixing.

plan.title: Solutions reveal
plan.detail: Compare with the exemplar solutions. Which bug was hardest to see and why? Log out.

successCriteria: I wrote a diagnosis before changing any code.
I fixed at least three of the four programs.
I can name a bug type I now recognise on sight.
lessons.moralDescription: The best learners admit what they do not know yet.
lessons.quote: Good, better, best. Never let it rest until your good is better and your better is best.
lessons.foodForThought: Is humility always easy, or does it sometimes take effort?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Individual practical + oral: demo the project and explain the code. Assessed on features, loops, conditions, variables and explanation quality.
lessons.sowResources: Marking rubric — from HTML: 'a multi-feature micro:bit Python project, explained clearly to peers'.
objectives: Demonstrate my multi-feature project working.
Explain the code clearly to the teacher.
Show where variables, loops and conditions are used.

plan.title: Brief
plan.detail: Assessment criteria on the board: features working, correct use of variables, loops, conditions, and quality of explanation.

plan.title: Final build time
plan.detail: Last chance to get features working. Silent conditions, technical help only.

plan.title: Demo and oral
plan.detail: One at a time: demo the device, then answer three questions about the code. Rest of the class continues polishing.

plan.title: Save the evidence
plan.detail: Final .hex saved with the correct name, plus a screenshot of the code.

plan.title: Close down
plan.detail: Devices counted in. Log out.

activities: Save code and screenshot as evidence
successCriteria: My project has at least two working features.
I used variables, a loop and a condition.
I explained the code without reading it out.
My evidence is saved correctly.
lessons.moralDescription: Give credit where it's due, and take feedback the same way you'd give it.
lessons.quote: A goal without a plan is just a wish.
lessons.foodForThought: Where in today's lesson could you practise fairness?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Add a third polish feature to the project (sound, animation, reset routine, welcome screen). Update the file to v3.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, micro:bit, feature-ideas menu. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Add a third feature that improves the user experience.
Keep the earlier features working.
Save the project as v3.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Polish that matters
plan.detail: From the feature-ideas menu: welcome screen, sound feedback, reset routine, low-battery warning. Choose based on what a real user would need.

plan.title: Build feature 3
plan.detail: Implement, then regression-test features 1 and 2.

plan.title: User test
plan.detail: Hand the device to someone who has never used it. Watch without helping. Note every hesitation.

plan.title: Save v3
plan.detail: Save and log the change in the dev diary. Log out.

successCriteria: My project has three working features.
The earlier features still work.
I watched a new user try it and noted what confused them.
lessons.moralDescription: Doing the boring warm-up daily is what makes the fun part possible.
lessons.quote: Character is doing the right thing when nobody's looking.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed self-discipline - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Design a one-page poster (Docs / Slides) explaining what the project does, who it's for, and how it works. Include a photo of the device.
lessons.sowResources: Google Slides / PowerPoint, class camera, poster template. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Design a one-page poster explaining my project.
Say who the project is for and how it works.
Include a photo of the device.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What makes a good poster
plan.detail: Look at the template: title, what it does, who it is for, how it works, photo. Rule: a reader should understand it in 30 seconds.

plan.title: Photograph the device
plan.detail: Apply Year 3 photography rules: good light, in focus, off-centre framing. Take three, choose the best.

plan.title: Build the poster
plan.detail: In Slides or Docs: insert the photo, write short sections, keep text large. No walls of text.

plan.title: 30-second test
plan.detail: Partner reads your poster for 30 seconds then explains your project back. If they cannot, the poster needs work. Log out.

successCriteria: My poster explains what the project does and who it is for.
It includes a clear photo of my device.
A partner understood it in 30 seconds.
lessons.moralDescription: Design for the person who will actually use what you make.
lessons.quote: Well begun is half done.
lessons.foodForThought: How would today's task go differently without empathy?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Rehearse a 3-minute presentation of the project. Peers give feedback: 'Was the code explanation clear?'.
lessons.sowResources: Presentation timer, peer-feedback sheet, class projector. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Rehearse a 3-minute presentation.
Explain the code section clearly.
Act on peer feedback before the showcase.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Presentation structure
plan.detail: One minute: what it is and who it is for. One minute: live demo. One minute: how the code works. Rehearse the transitions.

plan.title: Rehearse in threes
plan.detail: Each presents once, gets feedback from two peers using the feedback sheet. Focus question: was the code explanation clear?

plan.title: Act on the feedback
plan.detail: Adjust the poster or the script. Practise the weakest minute again.

plan.title: Timing check
plan.detail: Final run against the timer. Over-runners cut one sentence. Log out.

successCriteria: My presentation fits in three minutes.
My code explanation was rated clear by two peers.
I changed something based on the feedback.
lessons.moralDescription: A bug or a crash is information, not a verdict on you.
lessons.quote: It always seems impossible until it's done.
lessons.foodForThought: Who do you know that shows resilience well? What do they do?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Present projects to Year 5 (or another class). Save .hex + poster + demo photo to the portfolio folder. Ready for secondary!
lessons.sowResources: Class projector, portfolio folder, visitors' feedback slips. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Present my project to a younger audience.
Answer questions from visitors.
Save all my project evidence to the portfolio.

plan.title: Set up
plan.detail: Stations with device, poster and laptop showing the code. Invite Year 5 in.

plan.title: Project fair
plan.detail: Visitors rotate in small groups. Presenters give the 3-minute version, then answer questions. Half present, half host, then swap.

plan.title: Feedback read
plan.detail: Read the visitor feedback slips. Note the most common question - it shows what your explanation missed.

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: Save .hex, poster and device photo to the portfolio folder with correct names.

plan.title: Ready for secondary
plan.detail: Reflect: which skills carry into Year 7? Devices counted in. Log out.

successCriteria: I presented to visitors within the time.
I answered at least two questions about my project.
My .hex, poster and photo are in the portfolio folder.
lessons.moralDescription: Share what you have figured out - it does not run out.
lessons.quote: The expert in anything was once a beginner.
lessons.foodForThought: Is generosity always easy, or does it sometimes take effort?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Term theme: 'Office Mastery'. Introduce the Cambridge Computing pathway and Zera KS3 approach. Set personal WPM goals in TypingClub.
lessons.sowResources: KS3 overview slides, Cambridge Computing 0059/0860 syllabus overview, TypingClub goal sheet. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Explain how KS3 ICT leads into the Cambridge Computing pathway.
Set a personal WPM and accuracy goal.
Describe the term project and its deadlines.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: Baseline run: record WPM and accuracy for every pupil on the wall chart.

plan.title: Where this leads
plan.detail: KS3 overview slides: what Year 7-9 covers, and how it feeds Cambridge Computing 0059/0860 and IGCSE ICT 0417. Be concrete about why office skills matter at IGCSE.

plan.title: The term project
plan.detail: Theme: 'Office Mastery'. Reveal the linked mini-project - one topic, three files: a report, a spreadsheet and a deck, across Microsoft AND Google.

plan.title: Diagnostic task
plan.detail: 20-minute task: open Docs, type a structured paragraph with a heading, save to Drive with the correct name. Identifies who needs support with cloud files.

plan.title: Goals and deadlines
plan.detail: Write WPM goals on the goal sheet. Copy the four key deadline weeks into planners. Log out.

successCriteria: I recorded my baseline WPM and accuracy.
I completed the diagnostic and saved it correctly.
I can describe the three files in the term project.
lessons.moralDescription: Own your work, your files and your mistakes.
lessons.quote: A goal without a plan is just a wish.
lessons.foodForThought: Where in today's lesson could you practise responsibility?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: TypingClub: aim for 25+ WPM at 95%+ accuracy by half term. Track class average on a wall chart.
lessons.sowResources: TypingClub, WPM wall chart. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Reach 25+ WPM at 95%+ accuracy.
Type without looking at the keyboard.
Track my progress against the class average.

plan.title: Extended warm-up
plan.detail: Longer typing block today: 15 minutes of continuous practice with a posture check at the halfway point.

plan.title: Speed vs accuracy
plan.detail: Two timed runs: one all-out, one controlled. Calculate effective speed after corrections. The controlled run almost always wins.

plan.title: Targeted drills
plan.detail: Each pupil works on the letters their error report flags. TypingClub reports this per key - use it rather than generic practice.

plan.title: Class average
plan.detail: Update the wall chart. Calculate the class average WPM together - a live spreadsheet moment that previews Week 5.

plan.title: Touch-typing test
plan.detail: One exercise with a keyboard cover. Record the result separately - it is the honest number. Log out.

successCriteria: I completed a run at 95%+ accuracy.
I practised the specific keys I get wrong.
I typed a full exercise without looking down.
lessons.moralDescription: Ask 'why' and 'what if' - that is where real learning starts.
lessons.quote: Character is doing the right thing when nobody's looking.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed curiosity - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Styles, sections, an automatic Table of Contents. Compare Word's 'Styles' pane with Docs' 'Styles' menu — same idea, two tools.
lessons.sowResources: Microsoft Word, Google Docs, YouTube: Kevin Stratvert 'Word Styles', teacher demo. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Apply heading styles and section breaks.
Generate and update an automatic Table of Contents.
Compare how Word and Docs handle styles.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Styles properly
plan.detail: Modify a style rather than formatting text directly - change Heading 2 once and every heading updates. This is the professional workflow.

plan.title: Structure a long document
plan.detail: Open the practice text. Apply H1/H2/H3, add section breaks before major sections, then insert the Table of Contents.

plan.title: Same job, two tools
plan.detail: Repeat the essentials in Google Docs. Note the differences: no section breaks in the same way, TOC updates via a refresh button.

plan.title: Comparison table
plan.detail: Fill in a two-column comparison: Word vs Docs for styles and contents. Save both files. Log out.

successCriteria: My document uses modified styles, not manual formatting.
My contents list generates and updates automatically.
I can state two differences between Word and Docs.
lessons.moralDescription: Respect other people's work, ideas and privacy.
lessons.quote: Well begun is half done.
lessons.foodForThought: How would today's task go differently without respect?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Insert and format tables. Add captioned images. Add a short reference list using proper formatting.
lessons.sowResources: Word · Docs, printed reference-formatting exemplar. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Insert and format a table to a brief.
Add captioned images with automatic numbering.
Format a short reference list consistently.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Tables to a brief
plan.detail: Given a specification (5 columns, header row, banded rows, no wrapped text), build it exactly. Following a brief precisely is the IGCSE skill being seeded.

plan.title: Captions and figures
plan.detail: Insert two images with automatic captions. Discuss caption style: what the figure shows, not 'a picture'.

plan.title: References
plan.detail: Model a simple reference format: Author (Year) Title, URL, date accessed. Add three references for sources used, formatted identically.

plan.title: Brief check
plan.detail: Swap and mark a partner's work against the written brief - tick or cross only, no opinions. Log out.

successCriteria: My table matches every point in the brief.
My images are captioned and numbered automatically.
My three references use exactly the same format.
lessons.moralDescription: The best projects are built by people who help each other.
lessons.quote: It always seems impossible until it's done.
lessons.foodForThought: Who do you know that shows cooperation well? What do they do?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Enter data with clear headings. Use =SUM, =AVERAGE, =MAX, =MIN. Format as a table with alternating row colours.
lessons.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, formula reference card, sample class marks data. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Enter data with clear headings.
Use SUM, AVERAGE, MAX and MIN.
Format a range as a table with banded rows.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Anatomy of a spreadsheet
plan.detail: Cells, rows, columns, ranges. Rule: one heading row, one record per row, no blank rows in the middle.

plan.title: Four formulas
plan.detail: Enter the sample class marks data. Then =SUM(B2:B16), =AVERAGE, =MAX, =MIN. Show the colon meaning 'through' and dragging to select a range.

plan.title: Fill down
plan.detail: Use the fill handle to copy a formula down a column. Watch the cell references change - introduce the idea of relative references.

plan.title: Format as a table
plan.detail: Apply table formatting with banded rows and a bold header. Repeat the whole task in Google Sheets. Log out.

activities: SUM / AVERAGE / MAX / MIN on real data
successCriteria: My data has one clear heading row.
I used all four formulas correctly.
My range is formatted as a readable table.
lessons.moralDescription: Small, steady effort beats a rushed burst at the end.
lessons.quote: The expert in anything was once a beginner.
lessons.foodForThought: Is diligence always easy, or does it sometimes take effort?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Turn data into a bar and a pie chart. Add conditional formatting so scores > 80 are highlighted green.
lessons.sowResources: Excel · Sheets, chart-choice poster, conditional-formatting how-to. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Create a bar chart and a pie chart from the same data.
Choose the right chart type for the question.
Apply conditional formatting with a rule.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Which chart, and why
plan.detail: Bar for comparing amounts, pie for parts of a whole, line for change over time. Show a bad pie chart with 12 slices - the class will spot the problem.

plan.title: Build both charts
plan.detail: Select the range, insert a bar chart, then a pie chart. Add a title and axis labels - an unlabelled chart scores nothing.

plan.title: Conditional formatting
plan.detail: Rule: highlight scores above 80 in green, below 40 in red. Then change a value and watch the colour update live.

plan.title: Justify
plan.detail: Write one sentence: which chart answers the question better and why. Save both files. Log out.

successCriteria: My charts have titles and labelled axes.
I can justify my chart choice in one sentence.
My conditional formatting updates when data changes.
lessons.moralDescription: Sharing unfinished work for feedback takes courage - and pays off.
lessons.quote: Success is the sum of small efforts, repeated day in and day out.
lessons.foodForThought: Where in today's lesson could you practise courage?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Design principles: 1 idea per slide, minimal text, big font, consistent theme. Build a 5-slide deck.
lessons.sowResources: Microsoft PowerPoint, Google Slides, printed design principles handout, Duarte 'Slidedocs' free reference. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Apply slide design principles: one idea per slide, minimal text.
Use a consistent theme.
Build a 5-slide deck.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Death by PowerPoint
plan.detail: Show a slide crammed with bullet points, then the same content across three clean slides. Rules: one idea per slide, 6 words per line where possible, 24pt minimum.

plan.title: Build the deck
plan.detail: Five slides: title, context, main point, evidence, conclusion. Apply a single theme throughout.

plan.title: Contrast and images
plan.detail: Check text contrast against backgrounds; use one full-bleed image rather than three small ones.

plan.title: Three-second test
plan.detail: Flash each slide for three seconds. Can a partner say what it is about? Save in both PowerPoint and Slides. Log out.

successCriteria: Each slide covers one idea.
My deck uses a single consistent theme.
A partner understood each slide in three seconds.
lessons.moralDescription: Notice and thank the people who help you learn.
lessons.quote: Do not wait for the perfect moment. Take the moment and make it perfect.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed gratitude - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Save to Drive and OneDrive. Share a file with 'Comment' vs 'Edit' rights. Collaborate live with a partner on the same file.
lessons.sowResources: Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, sharing-permissions cheat sheet. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Save files to both Drive and OneDrive.
Share a file with Comment rather than Edit rights.
Collaborate live on one document.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Permissions matter
plan.detail: View, Comment, Edit - what each allows. Discuss a real scenario: sharing homework with a friend. Which permission, and why? Touches digital citizenship directly.

plan.title: Share and check
plan.detail: Share a document with a partner as Comment-only. The partner tries to edit and cannot - proof the permission works.

plan.title: Live collaboration
plan.detail: Change to Edit and both type in the same document simultaneously. Observe cursors, name labels and version history.

plan.title: Version history
plan.detail: Open version history and restore an earlier version. Powerful safety net - show it explicitly. Log out.

successCriteria: My file is saved in both Drive and OneDrive.
I shared a file with the correct permission level.
I co-edited a document and found version history.
lessons.moralDescription: Do the right thing even when nobody is checking.
lessons.quote: The only way to do great work is to love what you do.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Start the linked mini-project: a Report (Word / Docs) + a Spreadsheet (Excel / Sheets) + a Deck (PPT / Slides) on ONE topic. Plan today.
lessons.sowResources: Project brief handout, planning sheet, teacher exemplar. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Choose one topic that works across all three files.
Plan the report, spreadsheet and deck together.
Identify what data I need to collect.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: One topic, three files
plan.detail: Read the project brief. The three files must connect: the spreadsheet data appears as a chart in the report and in the deck. Show the teacher exemplar set.

plan.title: Topic selection
plan.detail: Topic must have numbers - screen time, canteen prices, sports results, travel to school. Reject topics with no data to chart.

plan.title: Plan all three
plan.detail: Planning sheet with three columns: report sections, spreadsheet columns and rows, slide titles. Plan them together so they line up.

plan.title: Data collection plan
plan.detail: Decide how to get 15+ rows of data before Week 13 - survey, measurement or published source. Log out.

successCriteria: My topic has numerical data I can chart.
My plan covers the report, spreadsheet and deck.
I know how I will collect at least 15 rows of data.
lessons.moralDescription: The best learners admit what they do not know yet.
lessons.quote: Mistakes are proof that you are trying.
lessons.foodForThought: Who do you know that shows humility well? What do they do?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Rotation: TOC in Docs, chart in Sheets, deck in Slides, cloud share. Peer-check against the marking rubric.
lessons.sowResources: Rotation stations, marking rubric shared with pupils, TypingClub. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Practise each exam skill under time pressure.
Peer-check work against the rubric.
Identify my weakest skill and practise it.

plan.title: Station briefing
plan.detail: Four stations, 15 minutes each, rubric at every station.

plan.title: Station 1 - TOC in Docs
plan.detail: Structure an unformatted text with styles and generate a contents list, against the clock.

plan.title: Station 2 - Chart in Sheets
plan.detail: From a given dataset: build a labelled chart and apply conditional formatting.

plan.title: Station 3 - Deck in Slides
plan.detail: Build three well-designed slides from supplied content.

plan.title: Station 4 - Cloud share
plan.detail: Save to both clouds with correct names and share with the right permission.

plan.title: Peer check and target
plan.detail: Peer-mark one station against the rubric. Write your weakest skill as a target. Log out.

successCriteria: I completed all four stations in the time.
I marked a peer's work accurately against the rubric.
I have named the skill I need to practise.
lessons.moralDescription: Give credit where it's due, and take feedback the same way you'd give it.
lessons.quote: A person who never made a mistake never tried anything new.
lessons.foodForThought: Is fairness always easy, or does it sometimes take effort?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Individual practical (90 min): produce a short report, spreadsheet and 3-slide deck on the same topic, saved to the cloud.
lessons.sowResources: Marking rubric — from HTML: 'a linked mini-project — a report, a spreadsheet and a deck — produced across Microsoft and Google'.
objectives: Produce a short report, a spreadsheet and a 3-slide deck on one topic.
Work across Microsoft and Google tools.
Save everything to the cloud with correct names.

plan.title: Brief
plan.detail: Read the task twice. 90 minutes, three files, one topic. Rubric visible. Silent conditions.

plan.title: Spreadsheet first
plan.detail: Data, formulas, chart. Doing this first means the chart is ready to embed - remind them of this strategy.

plan.title: Report
plan.detail: Structured with styles, a contents list, the embedded chart and a captioned image.

plan.title: Deck
plan.detail: Three slides: title, findings with the chart, conclusion.

plan.title: Save and submit
plan.detail: All three files saved to the cloud with the correct names, in the assessment folder.

successCriteria: All three files are on the same topic.
My spreadsheet has formulas and a labelled chart.
My report is structured with a contents list.
Everything is saved to the cloud correctly named.
lessons.moralDescription: Doing the boring warm-up daily is what makes the fun part possible.
lessons.quote: Well done is better than well said.
lessons.foodForThought: Where in today's lesson could you practise self-discipline?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Build the report: styles, TOC, at least one embedded chart from the spreadsheet, and a captioned image.
lessons.sowResources: Word · Docs, project brief. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Build the report section of the linked project.
Embed a chart from my spreadsheet.
Apply styles, a contents list and a captioned image.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Linked, not copied
plan.detail: Demo paste-linked vs paste-picture. A linked chart updates when the spreadsheet changes - show it happening live.

plan.title: Build the report
plan.detail: Introduction, three sections, conclusion. Apply styles, generate the TOC, embed the chart and add a captioned image.

plan.title: Structure review
plan.detail: Navigation pane check plus word count. Save to both clouds. Log out.

successCriteria: My report uses styles and an automatic contents list.
It contains a chart from my own spreadsheet.
It has at least one captioned image.
lessons.moralDescription: Design for the person who will actually use what you make.
lessons.quote: It is not that I'm so smart. I just stay with problems longer.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed empathy - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Build the spreadsheet: headers, at least 15 rows of data, SUM / AVERAGE, one chart and conditional formatting.
lessons.sowResources: Excel · Sheets, sample dataset (or pupil-collected data), rubric. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Build a spreadsheet with 15+ rows of real data.
Use SUM and AVERAGE correctly.
Add a chart and conditional formatting.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Clean data first
plan.detail: Headers in row 1, one record per row, consistent formats, no blank rows. Show what a messy sheet does to a chart.

plan.title: Build the spreadsheet
plan.detail: Enter the collected data, add formula rows for SUM and AVERAGE, format as a table.

plan.title: Chart and formatting
plan.detail: Insert a labelled chart. Add a conditional formatting rule that highlights something meaningful in your data.

plan.title: Rubric check
plan.detail: Self-check against the rubric, save to both clouds. Log out.

successCriteria: My spreadsheet has at least 15 rows of data.
SUM and AVERAGE calculate correctly.
My chart is labelled and my conditional formatting rule is meaningful.
lessons.moralDescription: A bug or a crash is information, not a verdict on you.
lessons.quote: Give me six hours to chop down a tree and I will spend the first four sharpening the axe.
lessons.foodForThought: How would today's task go differently without resilience?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Build the 5-slide deck: title, findings from the spreadsheet, one chart pasted from the spreadsheet, conclusion. Rehearse the talk.
lessons.sowResources: PowerPoint · Slides, deck template, presentation timer. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Build a 5-slide deck from my report findings.
Include a chart pasted from my spreadsheet.
Rehearse a timed talk.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Slides are not the report
plan.detail: The deck presents findings, it does not repeat the report. Cut ruthlessly - one message per slide.

plan.title: Build the deck
plan.detail: Title, context, findings with the chart, what it means, conclusion. Consistent theme, large text.

plan.title: Rehearse
plan.detail: Practise the talk twice with a partner and a timer. Speaker notes for the numbers, not the whole script.

plan.title: Peer feedback
plan.detail: Partner scores design and clarity, gives one fix. Apply it. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My deck has five slides with one idea each.
My chart came from my own spreadsheet.
I rehearsed within the time limit.
lessons.moralDescription: Share what you have figured out - it does not run out.
lessons.quote: The best way to predict the future is to create it.
lessons.foodForThought: Who do you know that shows generosity well? What do they do?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Present the linked project (3 files, 5 minutes). Save all three to the term portfolio folder.
lessons.sowResources: Class projector, portfolio folder, peer-feedback slips. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Present all three linked files in five minutes.
Show how the files connect.
Save the complete set to the term portfolio.

plan.title: Final checks
plan.detail: Update the TOC, check the chart appears in all three places, check file names.

plan.title: Demo day
plan.detail: Five minutes each in groups: show the report, then where the data came from, then the deck. Audience asks one question each.

plan.title: Peer feedback
plan.detail: Feedback slips: one strength, one improvement, focused on how well the three files connected.

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: All three files plus the PDF export into the term portfolio folder.

plan.title: Term reflection
plan.detail: Which tool do you now prefer, Microsoft or Google, and why? Log out.

successCriteria: I presented all three files within five minutes.
I explained how the files connect.
The complete set is in my portfolio folder.
lessons.moralDescription: One task done well beats five tasks half-done.
lessons.quote: Quality is not an act, it is a habit.
lessons.foodForThought: Is focus always easy, or does it sometimes take effort?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Term theme: 'Python — Decisions & Loops'. Recap Year 7 Python basics (input, print, variables). FIRST-TIME TEACHER TIP: Thonny's step-through debugger shows what's happening line-by-line.
lessons.sowResources: Thonny (thonny.org, free), Python recap worksheet, Isaac Computer Science account. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Recall Python basics: input, print and variables.
Run and step through a program in Thonny.
Describe this term's focus: decisions and loops.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: Baseline WPM run, posture check.

plan.title: Python recap
plan.detail: Work the recap worksheet: print(), input(), variables, int() conversion. The int(input()) pattern is the one they always forget - drill it now.

plan.title: Thonny tour
plan.detail: Editor, shell, variables pane. Run a short program, then run it again with the Debug button stepping line by line while watching the variables pane.

plan.title: Predict and check
plan.detail: Given three short programs, predict the output before running. Step through to see exactly where predictions were wrong.

plan.title: Term map
plan.detail: Theme: 'Python - Decisions & Loops'. Preview the mini-app project and the deadline weeks. Log out.

successCriteria: I can write a program that takes input and prints a result.
I stepped through a program watching variables change.
I know what the term project will be.
lessons.moralDescription: Ask 'why' and 'what if' - that is where real learning starts.
lessons.quote: Do not wait for the perfect moment. Take the moment and make it perfect.
lessons.foodForThought: Where in today's lesson could you practise curiosity?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Handle several cases with if / elif / else. Build a program that gives feedback on a test score band (fail / pass / merit / distinction).
lessons.sowResources: Thonny, printed if-elif-else reference, teacher-made exemplar. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Use if, elif and else to handle several cases.
Order conditions correctly.
Build a grade-band feedback program.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Why elif
plan.detail: Show four separate ifs versus if/elif/else. With separate ifs, several branches can run. Demo the bug before teaching the fix.

plan.title: Grade bands
plan.detail: Build: input a score, then fail under 40, pass 40-59, merit 60-79, distinction 80+. Watch for the classic bug: checking >40 before >80.

plan.title: Boundary testing
plan.detail: Test 39, 40, 59, 60, 79, 80. Boundaries are where the bugs live - make this a habit now, it pays off in Week 5.

plan.title: Peer swap
plan.detail: Run a partner's program with the boundary values and report any that behave wrongly. Log out.

successCriteria: My program uses if, elif and else.
Only one branch runs for any input.
My program gives the right answer at every boundary.
lessons.moralDescription: Respect other people's work, ideas and privacy.
lessons.quote: The only way to do great work is to love what you do.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed respect - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Use for loops with range() and while loops with a condition. Build a program that counts down from 10 to blast-off.
lessons.sowResources: Thonny, printed loops reference, YouTube: Craig 'n Dave 'Python Loops'. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Use a for loop with range().
Use a while loop with a condition.
Explain when each type of loop is the right choice.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Counted vs conditional
plan.detail: for = I know how many times. while = I keep going until something changes. Real examples: 10 press-ups vs run until the bell.

plan.title: range() in detail
plan.detail: range(5), range(1,6), range(10,0,-1). Print each to see exactly what it produces - the off-by-one confusion is best resolved by looking.

plan.title: Countdown to blast-off
plan.detail: Write the countdown with a for loop, then rewrite it with a while loop. Same output, two approaches. Add a sleep for effect.

plan.title: Infinite loop
plan.detail: Deliberately write one, watch it run, stop it with the red button. Discuss what was missing. Log out.

successCriteria: I wrote a working for loop with range().
I wrote a while loop that ends correctly.
I can say which loop suits a given problem.
lessons.moralDescription: The best projects are built by people who help each other.
lessons.quote: Mistakes are proof that you are trying.
lessons.foodForThought: How would today's task go differently without cooperation?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Combine conditions with and / or / not. Build a program that decides if someone can ride a rollercoaster (age >= 12 AND height >= 140).
lessons.sowResources: Thonny, printed truth-table handout. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Combine conditions with and, or and not.
Complete a truth table.
Build a program with a two-part entry rule.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Truth tables
plan.detail: Complete the handout for and, or, not. Key point: 'and' needs both true, 'or' needs at least one.

plan.title: Rollercoaster rules
plan.detail: Build: age >= 12 and height >= 140 to ride. Then a second version with or, and compare who gets in. The difference makes the operators concrete.

plan.title: not and negation
plan.detail: Rewrite a condition using not. Discuss which version reads more clearly - clarity is a real programming judgement.

plan.title: Test the rules
plan.detail: Test values that pass both, fail both and pass only one. Log out.

successCriteria: My program combines two conditions correctly.
I tested a case that passes one condition but not the other.
I can complete a truth table for and, or and not.
lessons.moralDescription: Small, steady effort beats a rushed burst at the end.
lessons.quote: A person who never made a mistake never tried anything new.
lessons.foodForThought: Who do you know that shows diligence well? What do they do?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Write a test plan before coding: what inputs to try, what outputs are expected. Test one program with normal, boundary and invalid inputs.
lessons.sowResources: Thonny, printed test-plan template (3 columns: Test Case / Expected / Actual). TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Write a test plan before writing code.
Choose normal, boundary and invalid test data.
Record expected versus actual results.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Three kinds of test data
plan.detail: Normal (typical use), boundary (edges), invalid (should be rejected). Model with an age-entry program: 25, 12, -3, 'banana'.

plan.title: Write the plan first
plan.detail: Using the 3-column template, write six test cases for a program that has NOT been built yet. Planning before coding is the point of the lesson.

plan.title: Build and test
plan.detail: Build the program, then run every test case and fill in the Actual column. Any mismatch gets investigated.

plan.title: What did the plan catch?
plan.detail: Share bugs found only because the test plan existed. Log out.

activities: Write a test plan before coding
Run tests and record actual results
successCriteria: My test plan has normal, boundary and invalid cases.
I wrote the plan before the code.
I recorded actual results and investigated mismatches.
lessons.moralDescription: Sharing unfinished work for feedback takes courage - and pays off.
lessons.quote: Well done is better than well said.
lessons.foodForThought: Is courage always easy, or does it sometimes take effort?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Build a number-guessing game: computer picks a number 1-100, user guesses, program says 'higher', 'lower' or 'correct'. Use a while loop and if / elif.
lessons.sowResources: Thonny, project brief, worked-example video (Isaac CS). TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Build a number guessing game with a while loop.
Give higher/lower feedback using if and elif.
Use a random number correctly.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Break down the problem
plan.detail: Decompose on the board: pick a secret number, ask, compare, respond, repeat until correct. Write the steps before any code.

plan.title: Build it
plan.detail: import random, randint(1,100), while guess != secret, if/elif for higher/lower. Support: a starter file with the loop skeleton for those who need it.

plan.title: Test with strategy
plan.detail: Play using binary search - always guess the middle. How many guesses should it take at most? A nice link to computational thinking.

plan.title: Extension
plan.detail: Count and display the number of guesses used. Save the file with a clear name. Log out.

successCriteria: My game picks a random secret number.
It gives correct higher/lower feedback.
The loop ends when the guess is correct.
lessons.moralDescription: Notice and thank the people who help you learn.
lessons.quote: It is not that I'm so smart. I just stay with problems longer.
lessons.foodForThought: Where in today's lesson could you practise gratitude?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Port the guessing game (simpler version, 1-10) to a micro:bit using MakeCode (toggle to Python view to see the same code).
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode (Blocks + Python view), micro:bit, MakeCode 'Python on micro:bit' guide. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Port a program from a computer to a physical device.
Adapt a design to hardware limits.
Compare MakeCode Python with desktop Python.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What has to change
plan.detail: The micro:bit has no keyboard and a 5x5 display. Discuss: how do you input a guess? How do you show higher/lower? Design constraints drive the redesign.

plan.title: Build the 1-10 version
plan.detail: Buttons increment the guess, A+B submits, arrow icons show higher/lower. Toggle to Python view and read the generated code.

plan.title: Compare the two
plan.detail: Side by side: desktop Python versus MakeCode Python. Same logic, different input and output.

plan.title: Demo
plan.detail: Swap devices and play a partner's version. Devices counted in. Log out.

successCriteria: My micro:bit version works with button input.
It shows higher/lower feedback on the display.
I can name two things the port forced me to change.
lessons.moralDescription: Do the right thing even when nobody is checking.
lessons.quote: Give me six hours to chop down a tree and I will spend the first four sharpening the axe.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed integrity - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Debug 3 teacher-made broken programs. Use Thonny's step-through: run one line at a time, watch variable values change.
lessons.sowResources: Thonny (Debug button), printed 'how to read a Python error' guide, buggy code files. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Read a Python error message and locate the fault.
Use Thonny's debugger to step through code.
Fix three broken programs systematically.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Reading errors
plan.detail: Anatomy of a traceback: the line number, the error type, the message. Cover NameError, TypeError, IndentationError and SyntaxError with an example of each.

plan.title: Debug three programs
plan.detail: Ten minutes each. Method: read the error, go to the line, step through with the debugger, form a hypothesis, change ONE thing, re-run.

plan.title: Bug taxonomy
plan.detail: Classify each bug: syntax, logic or runtime. Logic errors are the ones with no error message - the hardest kind.

plan.title: Share the trickiest
plan.detail: Which bug hid best, and what gave it away? Log out.

successCriteria: I can name the line and error type from a traceback.
I used the debugger to watch variables change.
I fixed at least two of the three programs.

resources.label: How to read a Python error - guide

lessons.moralDescription: The best learners admit what they do not know yet.
lessons.quote: The best way to predict the future is to create it.
lessons.foodForThought: How would today's task go differently without humility?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Add improvements: input validation (only accept numbers 1-100), a play-again loop, a score counter.
lessons.sowResources: Thonny, refinement checklist. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Add input validation to my program.
Add a play-again loop.
Track a score across rounds.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Never trust the user
plan.detail: What happens when someone types 'banana' into a number input? Crash. Introduce validation with a while loop and .isdigit() or try/except.

plan.title: Validate and loop
plan.detail: Add: reject anything not a number 1-100, and a play-again prompt that restarts the game while the answer is yes.

plan.title: Score counter
plan.detail: Add a variable counting games played and best number of guesses. Display it at the end.

plan.title: Break it
plan.detail: Swap with a partner and try to crash their program. Report anything that breaks. Log out.

activities: Input validation with a while loop
successCriteria: My program does not crash on invalid input.
The user can play again without restarting.
A score or best result is tracked and displayed.
lessons.moralDescription: Give credit where it's due, and take feedback the same way you'd give it.
lessons.quote: Quality is not an act, it is a habit.
lessons.foodForThought: Who do you know that shows fairness well? What do they do?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Rotation: (1) write a test plan for a partner's program, (2) find and fix bugs, (3) refactor for clarity. Prepare for the exam.
lessons.sowResources: Thonny, past-exam-style tasks, TypingClub. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Write a test plan for someone else's program.
Find and fix bugs under time pressure.
Refactor code to make it clearer.

plan.title: Station briefing
plan.detail: Three stations, 20 minutes each, exam-style tasks at every station.

plan.title: Station 1 - Write a test plan
plan.detail: For a partner's program: six test cases covering normal, boundary and invalid input.

plan.title: Station 2 - Find and fix
plan.detail: Two broken exam-style programs. Diagnose in writing, then fix.

plan.title: Station 3 - Refactor
plan.detail: Take working but messy code and improve it: better variable names, comments, remove repetition. Behaviour must not change.

plan.title: Exam readiness
plan.detail: Self-rate confidence on each skill; note the weakest for revision. Log out.

activities: Write a test plan for a peer's code
successCriteria: My test plan covers all three data types.
I diagnosed bugs in writing before fixing.
My refactored code behaves identically but reads better.
lessons.moralDescription: Doing the boring warm-up daily is what makes the fun part possible.
lessons.quote: You don't have to be great to start, but you have to start to be great.
lessons.foodForThought: Is self-discipline always easy, or does it sometimes take effort?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Individual practical: build a Python mini-app that meets a written brief and passes a written test plan. Show at least one bug found and fixed.
lessons.sowResources: Marking rubric — from HTML: 'a Python mini-app that passes a written test plan, with at least one bug found and fixed systematically'.
objectives: Build a Python mini-app that meets a written brief.
Pass my own written test plan.
Show one bug found and fixed.

plan.title: Brief
plan.detail: Read the brief twice. Requirements on the board: meets the brief, has a test plan, evidence of one bug found and fixed.

plan.title: Test plan first
plan.detail: Write the test plan before coding. This is assessed - remind them it carries marks even if the code is incomplete.

plan.title: Build
plan.detail: Silent conditions, technical help only. Circulate and note who is testing as they go.

plan.title: Test and evidence
plan.detail: Run every test case, fill in Actual, and screenshot the bug and its fix.

plan.title: Save and submit
plan.detail: The .py file plus the test plan into the assessment folder, correctly named.

activities: Test plan and evidence of debugging
successCriteria: My program does what the brief asks.
My test plan is complete with actual results.
I evidenced one bug found and fixed.
Both files are submitted correctly.
lessons.moralDescription: Design for the person who will actually use what you make.
lessons.quote: Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication.
lessons.foodForThought: Where in today's lesson could you practise empathy?

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Choose ONE project: quiz app, times-tables trainer, tip calculator or password strength checker. Write a plan with inputs, outputs and 3 test cases.
lessons.sowResources: Thonny, project menu card, planning template. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Choose a project and write a clear plan.
State the inputs and outputs.
Write three test cases before coding.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: The project menu
plan.detail: Quiz app, times-tables trainer, tip calculator, password strength checker. Discuss what makes each one hard - steer confident coders to the password checker.

plan.title: Plan it
plan.detail: Planning template: purpose, user, inputs, outputs, variables, the loop, the decisions.

plan.title: Three test cases
plan.detail: Write them now, before any code exists. Normal, boundary, invalid.

plan.title: Plan review
plan.detail: Teacher signs off each plan before coding starts next week. Log out.

activities: Write three test cases up front
successCriteria: My plan states the purpose, inputs and outputs.
I have identified the variables and the loop I need.
My three test cases are written before any code.
lessons.moralDescription: A bug or a crash is information, not a verdict on you.
lessons.quote: Debugging is twice as hard as writing the code in the first place.
lessons.foodForThought: Name one moment this week you showed resilience - or wish you had.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Build the project. Use variables, at least one loop and one if-block. Run against your own test plan.
lessons.sowResources: Thonny, test-plan template. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Build my mini-app from the plan.
Use variables, a loop and a condition.
Run my own test plan against it.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Build order
plan.detail: Get input working, then the core logic, then the loop, then the polish. Run the program after every small addition.

plan.title: Build
